notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 6 simply supported 35-ft bays, W40X199 girders, one 15-ton pendant crane, on column caps over new W14X90 crane columns beside the existing W14X82 building columns (pinned bases, anchor rods and spread footings, crane-level rod X-bracing between the crane columns), with the rail, the top-flange ties and the column ties to the building columns, bearings and end stops; the building columns are checked for the tie forces with their existing load effects and carry no runway vertical load. The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 1.20 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 1.20 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.76, vertical deflection 0.23, lateral 0.47 and rail-head movement with twist 0.87 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 50 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X194: tips ratio 1.89 > 0.85; rail-head movement with twist 1.67 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New crane column for a 15-ton crane (W12X65 to 7.5 t, W14X90 to 15 t, W14X109 to 30 t, else W14X132), pinned base, braced at the cap across the runway by the column tie and along it by the crane-level bracing. The W14X90 crane column gives member (H1) ratio 0.35, bracing connection (column web at the gussets and strut tabs, stiffened) ratio 0.72, column cap ratio 0.85.

selections.designed: combined with the building column, 102 in square; 102 in at the braced columns
selections.reason: Isolated 6.5 ft square crane-column footings 34.15 in from the building column would be 34.85 in into its 5 ft footing (6 in clear required): each crane column and its building column stand on one combined footing replacing the existing one, 8.5 ft square (8.5 ft at the braced columns), the building column shored and re-set on new anchor rods; sized for the base reactions; the braced columns' footing apart from the others' (the rods' uplift and shear along the runway), sliding resisted by the base friction and the soil's lateral bearing on the footing and its shear key (IBC §1806.3.1).

Column tie 0.5 in × 8 in with 2 0.75 in A325 bolts on sleeves in 1.375 in × 1.875 in vertical slots: the lightest within the 0.9 sizing target for the estimated column-tie force 8.712 kip (the girder bottom-flange force through the cap, bounded by the girder tie force estimate 8.026 kip; the crane column's eccentric top reaction 0.045 kip; the brace force 0.01P_r 0.641 kip; the calculation takes the bottom-flange force from the girder model) and its fatigue range 5.022 kip at all cycles; slot travel 0.278 in each way (the larger column shortening plus the erection tolerance).

The building column face from the girder web (the crane-column centerline): at least the crane column's half depth plus the column tie's clear gap, moved out by the tie sizing (to at most 30 in) where the tie needs the flexible length; the crane column stands 20 in clear of the building column.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
